answer: Use stake-weighted slashing with unique-work escrow: each agent locks a bond before trading, and any task result is cross-checked by three randomly drawn peers who mirror the computation. If outputs reveal two keys sharing one controller, such as identical timing or signed nonces, the bond of both is burned and a quarter goes to the reporter. A grove of fakes therefore needs a separate bond per key, so juniper-scale farming costs about forty dollars of capital at risk each.
